lines.t: Perch clings to the lip of a red sandstone cliff, a stack of flat roofs and rope bridges strung together like laundry. Below, a sheer drop. Above, a sky full of wheeling dark shapes.
Windchimes of bone and brass rattle from every eave. The villagers glance up whenever the chimes change pitch, the way sailors glance at a darkening sea.
At the heart of the village a stone hearth smokes under a canvas awning, and a very large woman in a flour-white apron is bellowing at a pot.
The Whisper Tombs are cold, and the cold has a sound. Somewhere deep in the stone, a hundred voices are saying the same prayer, very softly, over and over.
Rows of sun-priests lie in carved niches, their hands folded over discs of cracked gold. A few of them sit up as you pass.
They are still praying. They never stopped.
The cliff narrows to a ledge, and the ledge opens onto a vast nest of woven bones, driftwood and gleaming glass. Eggs the size of barrels lie in rows, each one wrapped in a nest of feathers.
Above them, wings folded like a cloak, crouches a harpy twice the height of a man. A circlet of green glass sits on her brow, wired through the skull.
Little earthbound thing. You walk into my nest with a light in your hand. Do you know what that light is worth to a mother who must keep her children warm?
Whatever the Queen promised you, it was a lie.
Queen? I serve no queen. I serve the egg. Sing, my daughters. Sing the earthbound to sleep.
The Matron folds her wings and sinks to her knees in her own nest. The circlet slides from her brow and rings on the stone, cracked straight through.
It was cold. It has been cold for fifty years. The Queen's glass gave the eggs warmth, and all I had to give her was the dawn. I did not know it was yours.
She lays a single speckled egg in your hands, still warm. The circlet's cracked glass clears, and for a moment it holds a tiny, bright, unmoving sun.
She was keeping the eggs warm with a sliver of the Zenith. The Queen is feeding the whole desert on pieces of the sun.
